conviction_note: No company-level Q3 number surfaced. The evidence is a peer and macro proxy on margin (FB Financial's NIM fell 12bp on deposit costs; the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16), a revenue bar of about $85.0M at the top of what the company's own H2 guide implies, and offsetting capital-return and insider-buying items. The findings sum to -0.25. p_up 48 on abs 2.3 gives -0.09. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because this name moved only +0.47% on a 14% core-EPS beat last quarter, so the lean is weak.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $1.31 and revenue $85.0M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EQBK/earnings-forecasts). Earnings Whispers has $1.32 and $85.03M (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/EQBK), so the two sources agree. The company's H2 2026 guide is in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526303176/eqbk-ex99_1.htm): NIM 4.25-4.35%, noninterest income $18-22M for the half (about $9-11M a quarter), noninterest expense $94-98M for the half (about $47-49M a quarter). Q2 NII was $73.9M at a 4.36% NIM. A $85M revenue bar therefore needs NII of about $74-76M with fees near the top of the guide, which puts it at or slightly above the guided midpoint. The EPS bar of $1.31-1.32 sits near my guide-midpoint rebuild: about $36M PPNR less roughly $2M provision, taxed at about 22%, over about 20.9M shares gives about $1.27-1.32. Q2 printed core EPS $1.41 against about $1.24, but revenue of $81.9M missed $84.9M.
positioning_check: Short interest was 591,717 shares at the 2026-09-30 record date: 3.36% of float, days to cover 5.5, up 18% from 500,858 on 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/EQBK/short-interest/, FINRA data published 2026-10-09). That is about double the 268,700 of Sep 2025. Lincoln Bancorp is private, so this is not merger-arb hedging. It is a rising but not crowded short. Options: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 186% of mid, OI 288), so there is no skew and no implied move. Tape: spot $46.48, -5.55% over 20d, -10.15% from the 52-week high, about -7% from the $49.85 deal reference price of 2026-09-02. The fall followed the Lincoln announcement (2026-09-03) and the Fed hike (2026-09-16).

findings.finding: Fed hike and FB Financial's margin squeeze point to EQBK's Q3 NIM landing in the lower half of its 4.25-4.35% guide (Q2 was 4.36%), leaving NII short of what a $85.0M revenue bar needs. FB Financial (FBK) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-13, after EQBK last spoke: NIM 3.83%, down from 3.95%, which it attributed to 'higher funding costs relative to earning asset yields'. FBK's interest-bearing deposit cost rose 7bp to 2.88% while its loan yield was flat at 6.21%. The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, so EQBK's Q4 margin guide is also open.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 revenue missed ($81.9M vs $84.9M) while core EPS beat 14%, and the stock moved +0.47% (baseline 2026-07-14). The market looked through a revenue/NII shortfall when expenses carried EPS. The worst reaction in the baseline is -6.63% (2025-07-14); I could not source which line drove it.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue consensus of $85.0M was not cut to the bottom of EQBK's own NIM guide; if the market expected margin pressure, the bar would sit near $83M. The stock is down 5.5% over 20 days, which partly prices sector rate risk, but the bar itself has not moved.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: a Tennessee peer with a different deposit mix, plus a macro event. EQBK has 8.0% brokered deposits, up from 5.7%, so its funding is rate-sensitive, but its 4.36% NIM includes $2.9M of accretion and higher loan yields. The Fed decision is a separate source (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm). The hike came late in the quarter, so it touches Q3 by only about two weeks. EQBK has not confirmed any of this.

findings.finding: The revenue bar of about $85.0M (Benzinga $85.0M, Earnings Whispers $85.03M) sits at the top of what EQBK's own H2 guide implies: NII of about $73-75M at a 4.25-4.35% NIM, plus $9-11M of quarterly fees. The same setup produced a revenue miss in Q2 ($81.9M vs $84.9M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by about 3.5% with a core EPS beat; the stock moved +0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Visible as a bar that was not trimmed after the Q2 revenue miss. Mostly priced, because the market reads core EPS here and EPS consensus of $1.31 sits near the guide midpoint. The landing would be inside the guided range.
findings.independence: The Q2 miss figures come from a separate source (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EQBK/earnings-forecasts). This shares its mechanism (NII) with the FBK margin finding but rests on different documents.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP results will be the first to carry Lincoln Bancorp deal costs. The Sept 3 announcement estimates about $23.7M of pre-tax merger charges, with close targeted for Q4 2026. The first call since the deal must defend 3.8% TBV dilution at close ($35.86 to $34.48), a 2.6-year earnback and a credit mark ranging from $18.0M (the base case) to $38.3M. The stock is about 7% below the $49.85 reference price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 carried $5.7M of Frontier merger expenses (GAAP $0.80 vs much higher core) and the stock moved -2.52% (2026-04-14). Frontier-related provisioning landed in that quarter too, so the cause is not isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: Merger costs are excluded from core EPS, which consensus tracks, so the main risk is a headline GAAP miss in automated coverage. The deal de-rating is largely in the price already (about -7% since Sep 2). A clean Lincoln credit update on the call could move it either way.
findings.independence: American Banker (https://www.americanbanker.com/news/kansas-community-bank-says-merger-will-enable-big-iowa-push, 2026-09-03) reports the deal and a positive Piper Sandler franchise view. Analyst views cited in search results flag TBV dilution. The two sources point in different directions.

findings.finding: A new 1,000,000-share buyback (about 4.8% of roughly 20.9M shares) took effect by 2026-10-01, after Kansas City Fed non-objection on 2026-08-05. Spot of $46.48 is near the $45.02 average EQBK paid in Q2. The Q3 report will show how much of the remaining 116,293 shares were bought at $45-48, and the call may signal pace under the new plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks were disclosed in the Q1 and Q2 releases (711,369 shares YTD at $44.84); the reactions were -2.52% and +0.47%, so no clear pattern.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public, so this is mostly priced. What is new is the execution pace near tangible book multiples close to where EQBK has been a buyer. A stock-funded deal pending a shareholder vote may restrict purchases, which caps the size.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000119312526303176/eqbk-ex99_1.htm) shows a history of buying at about $45. No other source.

findings.finding: Directors bought in the open market above today's price: D. Scott Rogerson bought 2,000 shares at $50.25 on 2026-07-31 and 2,000 at $50.00 on 2026-08-21; Lisa Schlehuber bought about 989 shares at $50.98 on 2026-07-28. CEO Brad Elliott's sales on 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-29 (6,913 and 4,165 shares at about $51) followed option exercises at $33.50.
findings.why_not_priced: Small-dollar director buys are public on EDGAR. They are a weak signal that insiders were not cautious about Q3 credit going into the quarter, and they predate the Lincoln deal.
findings.independence: The CEO's exercise-and-sell offsets them (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001227500/000165689226000008/primarydocument.xml). The net is weak.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 18% in the second half of September, to 591,717 shares (3.36% of float, 5.5 days to cover) at 2026-09-30. That is about 2.2x the September 2025 level, and it built after the Lincoln deal and the Fed hike.
findings.why_not_priced: It is published data and largely reflected in the 20-day drift. At 5.5 days to cover on 115k average daily volume, it could add squeeze fuel on a clean print; at 3.4% of float it is not crowded.
findings.independence: Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/eqbk/shortinterest) has older data showing about 3 days to cover in Sep 2025, which is consistent with the rise.

findings.finding: Q2 loan production was a record $315M and the pipeline rose to $1.6B. Management guided low-to-mid single-digit loan growth for H2 2026 after loans held for investment fell $22.6M in Q2 on acquired-portfolio runoff. Q3 is the first test of that promise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 had shrinking loans plus an EPS beat, and the stock moved +0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Guided and public. No Q3 balance-sheet data exists before the print (FDIC call reports come later), so the market cannot have seen the outcome. A growth number at the top of the range would land inside guidance.
findings.independence: This comes from a third-party call summary and is unconfirmed against the transcript. The Wichita Business Journal reported C&I loans rising from $766M to $958M year over year to Q1 2026 (equitybank.com repost). That predates Q3.

outside_window.finding: The Lincoln Bancorp close (Q4 2026, pending shareholder and regulatory approval) and the $750k consideration adjustment tied to the wind-down of Lincoln's LSBX BaaS platform by 2026-12-31.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The slight negative lean agrees with the -5.5% 20-day drift and the rising short interest, so whatever it carries is probably partly priced; that keeps p_up at 48, not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 2: the Lincoln merger charges are a below-core one_off with no path to the guide, so that finding went from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 6: the revenue bar would land inside the company's own guided range, so that finding went from -0.3 to -0.15.
Rule 1: Q2's 14% core beat bought only +0.47%, and the pipeline/loan-growth finding rests on a third-party summary, so it went from +0.2 to +0.15.
Rule 5: the FBK and Fed margin finding is a peer and macro proxy, so it went from -0.4 to -0.35. It stays filed with independence stating it is a proxy.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negative findings; 3.4% of float is not crowded, so nothing was shrunk on squeeze grounds.
abs_move_pct 2.3 and p_up 48 were left unchanged.
